title: Playing with her show behind the lines; the first date
summary: They play with a USO show near the front, and on their first date she pays for lunch.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But I do remember that she wasn't too hot on her jazz and everything like that. But the ballads were lovely and I fell for her right then and there. (LAUGHTER). So I played with her show. A guy from Chicago, Willie Show (Shearns) and his Bandwagon. And he knew me and of course all the musicians knew me and everything like that.
And she played a little accordion too, believe it or not. Because we used to go right behind the front lines. You could hear small arms firing you know

where we would play. We go out in the Ardennes Forest and play for these guys. I give those gals a lot of credit, they were right up there. Oh, I invited her out. I know, the first, we had a day off I invited her to go to Spa in Belgium. I said, we have a day off, do you want to go? Sure.

Well now I wasn't with my outfit. I was on a transfer you know. So I didn't have any money but I invited her out and when it came time to pay the bill for the lunch there I said, have you got any money I hope you have some money? (LAUGHTER). I said, I haven't got any money. I said, I haven't got paid by my outfit you know.
And on our first date she had to pay for it. I paid her back.
Well what would you have done if she hadn't had any?

I don't know what I'd have done. (LAUGHTER). You know in those days. I didn't care. If I'd have run into one of my buddies or someone. You could always get money from the guys. But that was the start of it. And after we played, and went into Aachen. Oh, here's what happened.
